entry: Jersey management and shared HTTP beans endpoint

questions.history: Request the beans endpoint on the management server.
questions.prediction: The PR reports that the separate server ignored the endpoint mapper. On the merge the response should be 200 and the bean’s scope should be `notelgnis`.
questions.basis: Reversing `singleton` gives that exact marker. The landed test checks a transformed scope in the HTTP response.
questions.refutation: The management endpoint fails, omits the known singleton, or reports its scope as `singleton` with the custom mapper installed.

questions.history: Omit `management.server.port`, keeping the same customizer, bean and application port discovery.
questions.prediction: The shared server should expose the reversed singleton scope on both revisions.
questions.basis: The earlier integration fixture already read a transformed scope on the shared port.
questions.refutation: The common-port response has an untransformed scope or no such bean.

questions.history: On the merge keep a named singleton bean and separate ports fixed. Register a second identifiable prototype bean in the configuration and inspect its entry in the same response.
questions.prediction: Both scope values should reflect the same mapping: `notelgnis` for the singleton and `epytotorp` for the prototype.
questions.basis: The custom serializer reverses every scope string. A parsed entry keyed by bean name associates the transformation with the correct bean.
questions.refutation: One transformed scope is present somewhere in the body but the named prototype reports `prototype`, is misidentified, or the JSON cannot be parsed.
